If blocking stops on its own

Some manufacturers stop background services to save battery. If that happens, allow BlockSocial to run in the background in your phone settings. This guidance is written from vendor documentation and has not been observed on a device by us.
How BlockSocial blocks an app
To interrupt an app the moment you open it, BlockSocial uses Android\'s Accessibility service.
Here is exactly what that means.
What BlockSocial reads. Only the name of the app that just came to the front, and the moment it happened. That is the whole list.

What BlockSocial never reads. Not the text on your screen. Not your messages. Not what you type. Not your passwords. The permission to read screen content is switched off in the app itself, so this is not a promise about our intentions — it is a setting the system enforces.

What BlockSocial does. When you open an app you chose to restrict, it shows you a full-screen pause with two options. If you choose to stay focused, it presses the home button for you. It never taps, types, or acts inside another app.
Where it goes. Nowhere. BlockSocial has no internet permission. Nothing about your apps or your choices leaves this phone.

A pause, not a wall

When you open an app you chose to restrict, BlockSocial shows a full-screen pause with two options: stay focused, or open it anyway for a few minutes. It is a moment to decide, not a lock you have to defeat.
You stay in control
You choose which apps are restricted and when. You can open a restricted app anyway at any time, turn any rule off, or uninstall BlockSocial. Nothing here works against you.
Everything stays on this phone
There is no account, no sign-in, and no internet permission. Your rules, your choices, and your history are stored on this phone and are deleted with the app.

What it enables. BlockSocial notices the moment a restricted app comes to the front and shows you the pause screen. Without it, nothing is blocked.
What is read. Only the name of the app that just came to the front, and the moment it happened. That is the whole list.

What is never read. Not the text on your screen. Not your messages. Not what you type. Not your passwords. Reading screen content is switched off in the app itself, so the system enforces this rather than us.
How to turn it off. Android Settings, Accessibility, BlockSocial. Or the Protection screen inside BlockSocial. Your rules and your history stay.
What it enables. Daily limits. BlockSocial can measure how long a restricted app has been in front today. Without it, schedules and always-on rules still work.
What is read. How long the apps you restricted were in the foreground, and when.
What is never read. Nothing inside those apps. No screen content, no messages, no notifications, no browsing.
How to turn it off. Android Settings, Special app access, Usage access, BlockSocial. Daily limits stop being measured; nothing else changes.
What it enables. BlockSocial can tell you when blocking has stopped working, so you find out from the app rather than from a missed block.
What is read. Nothing. This permission only lets BlockSocial show you a notice.
What is never read. Notifications from other apps. BlockSocial cannot see them.
How to turn it off. Android Settings, Notifications, BlockSocial. Blocking itself is unaffected.
